```{r}
#DATA PREP & DESCRIPTIVE STATS
library(readxl)
library(tidyverse)
library(survival)
library(survminer)

# Load Data
df <- read_excel("/Users/aryans/Downloads/Compiled Research Data FINAL (I hope).xlsx", sheet = "Master Dataset")

# Clean & Calculate Duration
df <- df %>%
  mutate(
    Closure_Year = as.numeric(str_sub(Closure_Quarter_Year, -4)),
    Duration = Closure_Year - Founding_Year
  ) %>%
  filter(Duration > 0)

df$Sector <- as.factor(df$Sector)

# Clean the Closure_Quarter_Year text string into a numeric decimal
df$Closure_Year_Num <- as.numeric(sub("Q._", "", df$Closure_Quarter_Year))
df$Quarter_Num <- as.numeric(sub("_.*", "", sub("Q", "", df$Closure_Quarter_Year)))

# Convert Q1 to .25, Q2 to .50, Q3 to .75, Q4 to 1.00
df$Closure_Decimal <- df$Closure_Year_Num + (df$Quarter_Num * 0.25)

# Calculate the Duration variable (Dependent Variable)
df$Duration <- df$Closure_Decimal - df$Founding_Year

# Run the Cox Model (Replicating your screenshot exactly)
library(survival)
model_baseline <- coxph(Surv(Duration, Event_Status) ~ GDP_Growth_YoY + CPI_Inflation + RBI_Repo_Rate + factor(Sector), data = df)
summary(model_baseline)

# Generate Descriptive Statistics
print("SUMMARY OF SURVIVAL DURATIONS")
summary(df$Duration)

print("EVENT STATUS BREAKDOWN (0 = Alive, 1 = Dead)")
table(df$Event_Status)

print("SECTOR BREAKDOWN")
table(df$Sector)

```

```{r}
# UNIVARIATE COX MODELS

# GDP Only
uni_gdp <- coxph(Surv(Duration, Event_Status) ~ GDP_Growth_YoY, data = df)
print("UNIVARIATE: GDP")
summary(uni_gdp)

# CPI Only
uni_cpi <- coxph(Surv(Duration, Event_Status) ~ CPI_Inflation, data = df)
print("UNIVARIATE: CPI")
summary(uni_cpi)

```

```{r}
#BASELINE MULTIVARIATE MODEL
model_baseline <- coxph(Surv(Duration, Event_Status) ~ GDP_Growth_YoY + CPI_Inflation + RBI_Repo_Rate, 
                        data = df, robust = TRUE)

print("BASELINE MODEL (MACROS ONLY)")
summary(model_baseline)
```

```{r}
# FULL MODEL (MACROS + SECTORS)
model_full <- coxph(Surv(Duration, Event_Status) ~ GDP_Growth_YoY + CPI_Inflation + RBI_Repo_Rate + Sector, 
                    data = df, robust = TRUE)

print("--- FULL MODEL RESULTS ---")
summary(model_full)
```

```{r}
# LIKELIHOOD RATIO TEST (FIXED)
# We fit temporary non-robust models purely for the ANOVA test

# Temporary Baseline Model (No robust=TRUE)
model_baseline_lrt <- coxph(Surv(Duration, Event_Status) ~ GDP_Growth_YoY + CPI_Inflation + RBI_Repo_Rate, 
                            data = df)

# Temporary Full Model (No robust=TRUE)
model_full_lrt <- coxph(Surv(Duration, Event_Status) ~ GDP_Growth_YoY + CPI_Inflation + RBI_Repo_Rate + Sector, 
                        data = df)

# The Likelihood Ratio Test
print("DOES SECTOR MATTER? (ANOVA TEST)")
anova(model_baseline_lrt, model_full_lrt)
```
```{r}
# THE FINAL PARSIMONIOUS MODEL
# Since sectors were insignificant, our final model relies only on the macro variables.
# We will use this model's coefficients for the final write-up.
model_final <- coxph(Surv(Duration, Event_Status) ~ GDP_Growth_YoY + CPI_Inflation + RBI_Repo_Rate, 
                     data = df)

print("FINAL MODEL RESULTS")
summary(model_final)

# Model Predictive Power (Concordance Index)
# A value between 0.5 (random guess) and 1.0 (perfect prediction)
print(paste("Concordance Index (C-index):", summary(model_final)$concordance[1]))
```
```{r}
#THE FUNDING WINTER STRUCTURAL BREAK

#Create the Funding Winter Dummy (2022 onwards)
df <- df %>%
  mutate(Funding_Winter = ifelse(Closure_Year >= 2022, 1, 0))

# Convert to a factor so R treats it as a dummy variable
df$Funding_Winter <- as.factor(df$Funding_Winter)

# Run the Structural Break Model (Interaction Term)
# The asterisk (*) tells R to test the Repo Rate, the Winter Dummy, AND their interaction.
model_break <- coxph(Surv(Duration, Event_Status) ~ GDP_Growth_YoY + CPI_Inflation + 
                       RBI_Repo_Rate * Funding_Winter, 
                     data = df, robust = TRUE)

print("FUNDING WINTER STRUCTURAL BREAK RESULTS")
summary(model_break)
```

```{r}
# DIAGNOSTIC ASSUMPTIONS
library(car)

#Multicollinearity (VIF)
dummy_lm <- lm(Duration ~ GDP_Growth_YoY + CPI_Inflation + RBI_Repo_Rate, data = df)
print("VIF TEST (Must be < 5)")
print(vif(dummy_lm))

#Proportional Hazards Assumption
ph_test <- cox.zph(model_final)
print("SCHOENFELD RESIDUALS (Global p must be > 0.05)")
print(ph_test)

# Plotting the residuals for the final model
plot(ph_test)
```

```{r}


library(gridExtra) # To arrange the plots together

# Extract the Martingale residuals from the NULL Cox model
# We use a null model (~ 1) because we are testing the functional form of the covariates against the baseline hazard
res_martingale <- residuals(coxph(Surv(Duration, Event_Status) ~ 1, data = df), type = "martingale")

# Add the residuals back to your main dataframe
df$Mart_Res <- res_martingale

# Set your smoothing span (Higher = Smoother. Default is usually 0.75. Try 1.0 or 1.2)
smooth_span <- 1.2 

# Build individual smoothed plots for each macroeconomic variable
plot_gdp <- ggplot(df, aes(x = GDP_Growth_YoY, y = Mart_Res)) +
  geom_point(alpha = 0.4, color = "black") +
  geom_smooth(method = "loess", span = smooth_span, color = "blue", se = TRUE) +
  theme_minimal() +
  labs(title = "GDP Growth", x = "Real GDP Growth (YoY)", y = "Martingale Residual")

plot_cpi <- ggplot(df, aes(x = CPI_Inflation, y = Mart_Res)) +
  geom_point(alpha = 0.4, color = "black") +
  geom_smooth(method = "loess", span = smooth_span, color = "blue", se = TRUE) +
  theme_minimal() +
  labs(title = "CPI Inflation", x = "CPI Inflation", y = "Martingale Residual")

plot_repo <- ggplot(df, aes(x = RBI_Repo_Rate, y = Mart_Res)) +
  geom_point(alpha = 0.4, color = "black") +
  geom_smooth(method = "loess", span = smooth_span, color = "blue", se = TRUE) +
  theme_minimal() +
  labs(title = "RBI Repo Rate", x = "RBI Repo Rate", y = "Martingale Residual")

# 4. Arrange them into a single clean graphic
grid.arrange(plot_gdp, plot_cpi, plot_repo, ncol = 1, top = "Smoothed Martingale Residuals of Null Cox Model")




```

```{r}
library(ggplot2)

# Extract deviance residuals
df$Dev_Res <- residuals(model_final, type = "deviance")

# Plot without the confusing LOESS curve
ggplot(df, aes(x = 1:nrow(df), y = Dev_Res)) +
  geom_point(alpha = 0.5, color = "black") +
  geom_hline(yintercept = 0, color = "green", linetype = "dashed") +
  theme_minimal() +
  labs(title = "Deviance Residuals (Outlier Detection)", 
       x = "Observation ID", 
       y = "Deviance Residuals")
```

```{r}
# KAPLAN-MEIER SURVIVAL CURVES BY SECTOR 
library(survival)
library(survminer)

#Fit the Kaplan-Meier Model
km_sector <- survfit(Surv(Duration, Event_Status) ~ Sector, data = df)

#Plot the Curves
print("--- PLOTTING KAPLAN-MEIER CURVES ---")
ggsurvplot(km_sector, 
           data = df,
           pval = TRUE,              # Calculates and displays the Log-Rank p-value
           conf.int = FALSE,         # Set to FALSE to keep the plot clean (5 confidence intervals gets messy)
           risk.table = TRUE,        # Adds a professional risk table at the bottom
           title = "Kaplan-Meier Survival Estimates by Mega-Sector",
           xlab = "Survival Duration (Years)",
           ylab = "Probability of Survival",
           legend.title = "Mega-Sector",
           ggtheme = theme_minimal())
```
